transcript:
Meeting Header: Date: 2027-04-25 15:42 UTC, Duration: ~52m
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Omar Reyes (Redwood SE), Priya Kapoor (Head of AI, Lattice), Jonas Meier (Infra), Evelyn Park (PM)

Auto-summary (auto): Kickoff for POC quality evaluation and workload scoping. Focus on golden prompts, regression, hallucination checks, scoring, and benchmarks.

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intros — i'm Maya, i'm the AE on this. Omar will walk through the technical plan.
[00:15] Priya: hi, priya here. thanks, excited to get the scope nailed down. small note, we need EU data residency for all logs.
[00:30] Omar: yep noted, that's on the private deployment / VPC side. we can run the pilot on our eu region or do a private plane on prem. the ask today is success criteria and workload size so we can size a realistic benchmark.
[00:50] Jonas: for infra context, our peak qps for the shopping assistant is about 150 qps during sales events, nominal 12 qps, average prompt length ~120 tokens.
[01:10] Evelyn: product wise we've got three flows: quick faq answers (short), product compare (multi-turn), and returns chat (sensitive PII). we want to catch hallucinations in compare flow especially.
[01:30] Maya: perfect. let's start with success criteria. priya, what does success look like for you in the 6-week pilot?
[01:45] Priya: technically: under 400ms p95 on the faq flow, hallucination rate < 2% on the golden set, and false-positive blocking of safe outputs under 1%. cost target is also important — something like less than x per 1k tokens but we can be flexible.
[02:10] Omar: quick callout: 400ms p95 is tight if you want high throughput with large context; we might recommend a variant with quantization and a shorter context or dedicated capacity for the high-traffic windows.
[02:30] Jonas: where's the tradeoff? dedicated vs hosted? we prefer hosted for speed of setup but if dedicated reduces cost at scale maybe we'll go that route.
[02:45] Maya: yep, we typically present two paths: hosted (fast onboarding, pay-as-you-go) or Dedicated (reserved GPUs for steady high qps). for the pilot we can run hosted benchmarks first, then test a dedicated sim if numbers indicate.
[03:05] Priya: ok that sounds fair. what's your golden prompts approach? how many prompts do you want?
[03:20] Omar: our standard is 100-300 golden prompts covering normal, edge, and adversarial cases. for this flow given the variety, i'd recommend 200: 120 normal, 50 edge, 30 adversarial. we also include format checks and hallucination probes.
[03:40] Evelyn: format checks meaning?
[03:50] Omar: like we assert structure of responses — e.g., for product compare we expect a table-like output, certain fields present. if model diverges we flag a format fail. also we run hallucination detectors that check factuality against product catalog and local db.
[04:10] Priya: and regression tests? how do those get run ongoing?
[04:20] Maya: we build a regression playlist. during the POC we run nightly regression on the golden set, and pre/post-rollout comparisons. we can attach automated scoring and a dashboard so you see drop in accuracy or increases in hallucination.
[04:35] Jonas: about the hallucination checks — do you do external retrieval checks or do you rely on model-only heuristics?
[04:45] Omar: both. we use retrieval-augmented checks where applicable — cross-check outputs against canonical product data via small-to-medium sized queries. for some cases we run statistical heuristics that catch improbable entity insertions.
[05:05] Priya: sensitive data redaction — we need KMS integration and no logs stored outside eu.
[05:15] Maya: understood. we support KMS and can limit logs to eu; for the hosted option we have an eu region with data residency controls. for Private we can do customer-managed keys and no control-plane retention.
[05:35] Evelyn: timeline question — how long to set up a pilot and run benchmarks?
[05:45] Omar: typical: 5 business days to spin up an env on hosted, a couple extra for private. then we'll run a warm vs cold benchmark run — warm meaning with cache and kv primed, cold meaning first-request latency. each run takes 1-2 days to gather steady-state metrics if you want robust numbers. so overall 3-4 weeks to a full benchmark + analysis.
[06:10] Priya: can we compress that? we aim for a 6-week pilot window but need a decision by week 4.
[06:20] Maya: we can prioritize a quick 48h smoke benchmark to unblock decisions then run extended tests in parallel.
[06:30] Jonas: sizing — what do you need from us to simulate realistic load?
[06:40] Omar: qps profile (you gave peaks), distribution of context lengths, and a sample of real queries (200 sample golden plus an anonymized 2k logs sample for load testing). also token length distribution — we need to choose batch sizes and kernel optimizations.
[06:58] Priya: we can provide 200 golden samples and export 2k anonymized logs by monday.
[07:08] Evelyn: scoring approach — how do you compute hallucination rate?
[07:20] Omar: for factual outputs we compare model facts against the canonical data; if a free-form sentence contains facts not found in the source we mark it. we also score on BLEU / ROUGE style overlap for structured fields, and a human-in-the-loop label for a subset to calibrate thresholds. numeric scoring combined into a composite score: availability/latency (weighted), accuracy/hallucination (weighted higher), and format compliance.
[07:50] Maya: to be concrete we propose weights: 40% hallucination/accuracy, 30% latency (p95), 20% format/regression pass rate, 10% cost efficiency. happy to adjust.
[08:05] Priya: that weighting seems reasonable, maybe shift latency to 25% and cost to 15% but we can iterate.
[08:15] Omar: fine. we'll put an editable rubric in the doc we share.
[08:25] Jonas: benchmarks — can you simulate cold-starts? our infra sees cold bursts when a new version of the assistant deploys.
[08:35] Omar: yes, we do cold start runs with KV empty and measure first-token latency and p95 over the first 10 min. warm runs prime the KV cache. we'll also run sustained qps tests to measure throughput and cost-per-token.
[08:55] Priya: cost numbers — can you give a back-of-envelope for 150 qps peak?
[09:05] Maya: we need to pick a model profile. for example, a performance-tuned 8-bit quantized variant costs X per hour on Dedicated; hosted varies. we'll include two cost scenarios in the doc: optimistic (quantized) and conservative (fp16/dedicated).
[09:25] Priya: ok. also we want the golden prompts to include negative tests that try to elicit hallucination. ethical/legal want examples flagged.
[09:40] Omar: we'll include adversarial prompts and a set of red-team style inputs that try to coax invented facts, plus PII leakage probes.
[09:55] Evelyn: on regression — if a regression is detected, what's rollback policy?
[10:05] Maya: for the POC we recommend automatic rollback for severe regressions (e.g., >5% delta on hallucination) and manual review for smaller drops. Redwood Console will surface alerts.
[10:20] Priya: SSO & audit log question — we need SAML and audit logs delivered to our SIEM.
[10:30] Maya: supported. we'll include SSO config steps and a log forwarder for the POC.
[10:40] Jonas: data retention policy — can we have minimal retention on the control plane?
[10:50] Omar: yes, we can set minimal retention. for private we can disable control-plane logging entirely. hosted we have retention settings down to 7 days and EU-only storage.
[11:05] Maya: ok so let's capture concrete success criteria: p95 < 400ms on faq, hallucination < 2% on golden set, format pass > 98% for structured flows, cost under internal threshold (we'll put a placeholder). anybody object?
[11:20] Priya: sounds good, need that formalized in the doc.
[11:25] Omar: next, golden prompt selection — we'll provide the template: input, expected structured output, pass/fail rules, and an explanation. you can add labels for privacy sensitive.
[11:40] Evelyn: can we include a human review bucket for borderline cases?
[11:45] Omar: yes, the scoring pipeline tags low-confidence results for human review and we can estimate review volume w/ your sample data.
[11:55] Priya: volume — what's the expected human review rate initially?
[12:05] Omar: depends on threshold, but for a tuned rollout we aim for < 0.5% of queries in human review for normal flows. adversarial flows may be higher.
[12:20] Maya: timeline recap — we propose: this week share golden template + rubric, customer shares 200 golden + 2k anonymized logs by Mon 2027-05-03, Redwood runs smoke benchmark within 48h, full warm/cold runs week of 2027-05-10, then results + cost analysis by 2027-05-17.
[12:45] Jonas: question on perf metrics — do you provide token-level breakdowns?
[12:55] Omar: yes, console provides token latency, kv hits, batch sizes, and per-route cost. we'll attach sample dashboards.
[13:05] Priya: any blockers from your side?
[13:10] Maya: none at the moment, just waiting on the sample data and qps confirmation.
[13:20] Priya: ok we'll get the files and open an internal ticket to expedite.
[13:30] Evelyn: regarding compliance docs — can you send SOC2+ISO exports?
[13:35] Maya: we'll include SOC2 and GDPR data processing addendum, plus KMS notes.
[13:45] Omar: i'll prepare the benchmark config (batch sizes, sequence lengths, kernel flags) and share as an annex.
[13:55] Maya: any final questions?
[14:05] Jonas: none here.
[14:10] Priya: one last: can we test with our retrieval layer in the warm run?
[14:15] Omar: yes, we can wire your retriever; just provide access credentials and an index snapshot for the test.
[14:25] Maya: great. recap of next steps — we will: share golden prompt template & rubric, share estimated cost scenarios, run smoke benchmark after we get samples, schedule the deep benchmark and send calendar invite for May 11th.
[14:45] Priya: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity.
[14:50] Maya: thanks all. we'll follow up by email with the artifacts.
[14:55] (call ends)

Notes on transcript fidelity: occasional mislabels and ASR errors present — e.g., "Redwood Dedicatd" instead of "Dedicated" in one auto-gen snippet.
